packs.title: Bay, Hills and Layers
packs.promise: Connect Naples from museum rooms to hill gardens, waterfront edges and working transit.

q.s: Turn the palace’s repeated openings into a visual rhythm, then change one beat on paper.
st: From an open edge of Piazza del Plebiscito, choose two neighbouring openings on the palace facade and notice the gap between them.
Give the opening and the gap a simple mark each, then repeat the pair across a short strip of paper.
Below it, make a second strip with one gap widened or one opening turned. Label this as your invention and note how the rhythm changes.

q.s: At Molo Beverello, make a short Naples–Capri route card using the operator’s scheduled departure and what you can see from a public port edge.
st: On NLG’s Naples Beverello–Capri route page, choose one current scheduled departure and record its date, time and destination.
At an open public edge of Molo Beverello, note whether a vessel or departure activity is visible; keep out of queues and restricted areas.
On the route card, separate the schedule from what you observed. If nothing is visible, write “not observed” rather than inventing a sailing.

q.t: A Tree Archive in the Bosco
q.s: Follow one open Bosco avenue and compare the planted edge with a built feature that frames it.
st: At an open Real Bosco di Capodimonte avenue, choose a short accessible segment and note the line made by planted forms.
Find a building, fountain or path junction along that segment; compare its shape with the planted line.
Write a two-part field note: what was intentionally aligned and what has grown or changed.

packs.title: Ancient Grid and Living Streets
packs.promise: Read Naples’ compact historic center through streets, courtyards, churches and public movement.

q.s: On Spaccanapoli, draw how a narrow street frames a slice of sky between its two building edges.
st: Find a safe, open stretch of Via Benedetto Croce or Via San Biagio dei Librai.
Draw the two opposing building edges and leave the sky gap blank; include a doorway or balcony only if it helps show scale.
Add one line explaining how the narrow street changes the shape of the visible sky.

q.t: Two Marks in Piazza del Gesù
q.s: In Piazza del Gesù Nuovo, use the obelisk and the church’s faceted stone facade as two different orientation points.
st: From an open piazza edge, locate the tall obelisk and the patterned facade of Gesù Nuovo.
Turn once between them and record which landmark is easier to find above a crowd and which requires looking closer.
Write a two-column orientation note with one reason for each choice.

q.s: Inside Santa Chiara’s cloister, compare a tiled pillar with the garden walk it borders.
st: Check current admission and access rules, then enter the Chiostro Maiolicato visitor route.
Choose one painted pillar and one adjacent garden path; note how the pillar’s color or scene meets the planted space.
Write a two-part note: one detail on the ceramic surface and one spatial relationship to the path.
